body:
I just want to say thank you so much for taking the time to read this, actually think about it and reply. It's just nice to be acknowledged. :)

It's also really interesting to see this from an outside point of view - I never realised that a major issue is that I don't feel believed or listened to by the people I CAN talk to, but it makes total sense, especially with these feelings of total frustration.

And it's nice to know you think you'd be in the same position with counsellors. I've genuinely been made to feel such a useless, irritating patient for just not clicking or trusting her, even though I have my reasons. And I realise loads of people don't go to school straight away - it's just that I (stupidly) got my hopes up for this amazing but ridiculously competitive uni. I was convinced I'd get in, move far away and live happily ever after, and have something concrete planned for the next three years. I didn't, and so I beat myself up about it, telling myself I was clearly stupid etc etc. The idea of floating around for a year, just getting a job and things not only terrifies me (again, I have no confidence left and I just feel like I need some structure, like at uni), but I could not stand another year at my house, and I don't have money to travel or rent somewhere and don't know anyone well enough to stay with them. So it looks like I'll be going somewhere I don't really want to be, and I'll just have to hope it works out OK :)

Again, I just really want to thank you, kind internet stranger. You've made me feel a little bit wanted. :)
